description: I am a 3rd-year CSE student specializing in AI & ML, passionate about innovation, problem-solving, cybersecurity, web development, and space technology. I’m building a collaborative team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to develop impactful solutions. Looking for passionate teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, web development, data analysis, research, UI/UX, and presentation. Let’s learn, innovate, and turn ideas into reality!
summary:
ASTRA HEALTH 360 is a project developed to make astronaut health monitoring easier and help improve safety during space missions. We wanted to create a single platform where important crew health information and mission-related updates could be viewed and managed in one place.

Our website monitors basic health parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen level (SpO₂) and body temperature using sensor data and simulated readings. It also includes a Mission Intelligence feature that uses machine learning to identify unusual health patterns and alert the team when something may need attention.

To make the project more relevant to space research, we have included four NASA-related datasets covering metabolic, immune and cardiovascular studies. Along with this, the website offers an AI assistant, fitness and wellness tracking, medical inventory, environmental monitoring, ISS tracking and satellite communication features.

We built ASTRA HEALTH 360 using Python, Flask, HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SQLite. Through this project, our aim is to bring health monitoring, AI and space research together in a simple and useful platform that can support astronaut well-being and safer space missions.
details:
ASTRA HEALTH 360 – Astronaut Health Monitoring and Mission Support System

ASTRA HEALTH 360 is a project developed to make astronaut health monitoring and mission support easier through AI and technology. During space missions, astronauts face different health and environmental challenges. Our main idea is to bring important health monitoring and mission support features together in one platform.

What does our project do and how does it work?

Our platform has a dashboard where users can view important health details such as heart rate, SpO₂ and body temperature. It displays health readings and provides alerts when unusual values are detected.

We have also used Machine Learning with the Isolation Forest algorithm to identify unusual patterns in health data. An AI assistant is included to help users interact with the platform and get relevant information.

Some of the main features we developed are:

  • Health Monitoring: Displays heart rate, oxygen levels, body temperature and health alerts.
  • AI and ML: Uses machine learning to identify unusual health patterns and an AI assistant for user support.
  • Fitness and Wellness: Provides features related to astronaut fitness and well-being.
  • Medical Inventory: Helps keep track of important medical supplies.
  • Environmental Monitoring: Displays environmental information relevant to space missions.
  • ISS Tracking: Shows publicly available information about the International Space Station.
  • Satellite Communication: Includes a simulated communication interface for mission support.
  • NASA Research Data: We integrated four research datasets – metabolic.csv, immune_eve.csv, immune_alamar.csv and cardiovascular.csv.

Benefits and Impact

The main benefit of ASTRA HEALTH 360 is that it brings multiple astronaut health and mission support features into one place. It helps users monitor health information, identify unusual readings, manage medical supplies and access important mission-related information.

Through this project, we aim to contribute to better astronaut health awareness and support safer human space exploration in the future.

Technologies Used

We developed this project using the following technologies:

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend.
  • Python and Flask for the backend.
  • SQLite for database management.
  • Scikit-learn for Machine Learning and Isolation Forest.
  • OpenRouter for AI assistant integration and Ollama for Llama 3.2 experimentation.
  • Three.js and HTML Canvas for visual elements.
  • NASA-related research datasets in CSV format.
  • Visual Studio Code for development.
  • GitHub for version control and Render for deployment.

What makes our project different?

The main idea behind our project is to combine different features that are useful for astronaut health and mission support into a single platform. Instead of having separate sections for health monitoring, AI assistance, fitness, medical inventory and ISS tracking, we have brought them together with a common dashboard.

We focused on making the platform simple to use while including useful technologies such as AI, Machine Learning and data visualization.

Factors Considered

While developing this project, we considered astronaut safety, health monitoring, ease of use, data visualization and the difficulties astronauts may face during long-duration space missions. We also focused on making the platform modular so that additional features can be included in the future.

Our current prototype uses simulated IoT health readings and a simulated satellite communication interface. It also uses research datasets and publicly available ISS information. The platform is a prototype and is not intended to provide medical diagnoses or actual satellite communication.

Our Goal

Through ASTRA HEALTH 360, we want to explore how AI, Machine Learning and modern web technologies can be used to support astronaut health and make future space missions safer.
